affordance_in_statement: The physical arrangement of the network guarantees a specific structural property: any closed loop of interfering devices ... will always consist of an even number of devices.
secondary_shortcut_name: Kőnig reduction to maximum independent set
removal_suggestion: There is no wording-only removal that preserves the task's mathematical structure: the even-cycle promise is exactly what makes the graph bipartite. If the promise must remain, present it only indirectly through the physical scenario rather than explicitly describing all cycles as even.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes the even-cycle promise as bipartiteness, then uses bipartition/matching machinery to obtain a maximum independent set and select k vertices.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: any closed loop ... will always consist of an even number of devices

common_affordance: The explicit promise that every cycle has even length, allowing immediate reduction to a bipartite graph

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Although it also attempted a Hopcroft–Karp-based bipartite solution, its matching or independent-set reconstruction is incorrect on some valid instances.
It identifies bipartiteness but appears to rely on a color-class shortcut rather than correctly handling the maximum independent set when vertices from both sides are needed.
It similarly builds the two color classes, but its incomplete/incorrect bipartition-based construction does not correctly solve all target-size cases.

recommended_edit: Do not state the even-cycle property directly; encode the same promise indirectly in the physical scenario, so the solver must establish or infer bipartiteness instead of obtaining it immediately from the statement.
regression_risk: This may restore models that already know the equivalent odd-cycle characterization or that test bipartiteness directly from the input.
